content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Summary:** Article 12's mutual indemnities fail the INDEMN fallback. SFJ's indemnity (12.1.1(a)–(f)) covers only its gross negligence/wilful misconduct, breaches of the Agreement, Protocol and AZ License, and post-Program-Transfer trial/product liability — no third-party IP infringement at all. Worse, PB's indemnity at 12.1.2(f) is a one-way IP indemnity that reaches infringement caused by "either Party" in performing its duties, so PB currently protects SFJ for SFJ's own conduct. That is walk-away territory under the rule.

**Redline (fallback level, validated ok:true):**
1. New Section 12.1.3 — SFJ IP indemnity of the PB Indemnified Parties, with the customary PB-modification / PB-combination / PB-specification exclusions, procure–modify–replace remedies with a refund backstop, and a 3× annual Approval Payments super-cap scoped to the new indemnity only (so SFJ's existing uncapped indemnities are not weakened).
2. 12.1.2(f) narrowed from "either Party" to "PB" — removes the circularity with the new SFJ indemnity.
3. 12.2.1 cross-reference conformed to include 12.1.3 so the existing notice, control-of-defence and cooperation machinery applies.
